versions.text: Criterion: Verify that the structures, equipment, and equipment provisions in, adjacent to, or immediately downstream of cavities open to the airstream during flight are designed for the effects of oscillatory air forces. Standard (Army and Air Force): a. All aeroacoustic loads sources associated with the air vehicle and its usage are identified. b. The airframe is designed such that an uncertainty factor of +3.5dB is applied on the predicted aeroacoustic sound pressure levels. c. The airframe is designed for fatigue life such that a factor of 2.0 is applied on the exposure time derived from the air vehicle specified service life and usage. Standard (Navy): Airframe is designed such that pressure oscillations within and downstream of cavities are minimized by the addition of air flow devices, where practicable. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analyses and tests. The following compliance instruments are applicable in addressing the standards: a. Predictions of the cavity aeroacoustic loads and fatigue life encompassing the air vehicles service life and usage. b. Wind tunnel models that define acoustic levels. c. Component acoustic fatigue tests based on fatigue life predictions. d. Ground and flight aeroacoustic measurements from full scale test aircraft. References: (Navy/Air Force fixed wing) JSSG-2006: A.3.3.9, A.4.3.9 (Army rotary wing) ADS-10-SP, ADS-24 (cancelled), ADS-27-SP, ADS-29 (cancelled), ADS-51, ADS-64-SP (inactive), AR-70-62 (Navy rotary wing) As identified in the AVPS Addendum for the respective air vehicle and/or AR-56, AR-89, MIL-D-23222 14 FAR 23, 25, 27, 29 STANAG 4671: USAR 321
